We need to generate JUnit 4 test cases to comprehensively test all methods in OneOfValidator. The class depends on many other classes: BaseJsonValidator, JsonSchema, ValidationContext, ExecutionContext, CollectorContext, Scope, ValidatorState, ValidationMessage, JsonSchemaException, etc. To test OneOfValidator in isolation, we could use mocks (e.g., Mockito) to simulate behavior. Provide tests for constructor (ensuring schemas added), validate method (various scenarios: exactly one schema matches, zero matches, multiple matches, failFast behavior, state flags), walk method (when shouldValidateSchema true/false), preloadJsonSchema (calls initializeValidators). Also test resetValidatorState indirectly via validate.

We'll need to create stub/mock classes for dependencies. Since we are writing test code only, we can use Mockito to mock interfaces. Provide a test class OneOfValidatorTest with @RunWith(MockitoJUnitRunner.class) or use @Before to init mocks.

We need to ensure coverage of:

- Constructor builds schemas list based on schemaNode (a JsonNode array). We'll mock JsonNode to return size and child nodes.

- validate: scenario 1: exactly one schema validates (returns empty set). Expect no errors, state matchedNode true.

- scenario 2: zero schemas validate (all return non-empty errors). Expect error message with numberOfValidSchema =0, errors contain childErrors.

- scenario 3: more than one schema validates (two schemas return empty). Expect short-circuit after >1, error message numberOfValidSchema >1, errors contain child errors? Implementation adds errors only when numberOfValidSchema !=1, includes childErrors (which may contain errors from schemas that had errors). Since we break after numberOfValidSchema >1, childErrors may include errors from previous schemas (including those that matched?). In scenario where two schemas match and have empty errors, childErrors would be empty. So errors will just contain validationMessage.

- test failFast: set failFast true on validator (BaseJsonValidator? Probably has a field). We'll need to instantiate OneOfValidator via constructor; maybe we can set the protected field via reflection or subclass? The BaseJsonValidator may have a protected boolean failFast; we can set using reflection.

- test walk: when shouldValidateSchema true, it should call validate and return its messages. When false, it should call walk on each child schema but not collect messages.

- test preloadJsonSchema: ensure each schema's initializeValidators called.

Need to mock CollectorContext, ExecutionContext, JsonSchema, ValidationContext, etc.

Simplify: create a TestHelper inner class that extends OneOfValidator to expose schemas list for verification.

But we can just use reflection to get private schemas field.

Implementation details:

- Mock ValidationContext to return new JsonSchema mock when newSchema called. We'll need to stub validationContext.newSchema(...). We'll create a mock JsonSchema that we can configure per index.

- The constructor loops over schemaNode size and calls validationContext.newSchema. So we need to set up behavior: when validationContext.newSchema(anyString(), any(JsonNode.class), any(JsonSchema.class)) return appropriate mock schema (e.g., schemaMocks[i]).

- Provide JsonNode schemaNode mock: size returns N, get(i) returns childNode mock (could be same for all). Provide childNode as mock JsonNode.

- ExecutionContext mock returns CollectorContext via getCollectorContext.

- CollectorContext mock: need methods enterDynamicScope, exitDynamicScope, get(key), getEvaluatedItems, getEvaluatedProperties. We'll create simple mock for Scope (maybe just a mock). For simplicity, we can have collectorContext.enterDynamicScope return a mock Scope, and exitDynamicScope also return a mock Scope. The mergeWith method called on Scope; we can stub it to do nothing.

- CollectorContext.get(ValidatorState.VALIDATOR_STATE_KEY) returns a mock ValidatorState. We need to stub methods: setComplexValidator, setMatchedNode, isWalkEnabled, isValidationEnabled, hasMatchedNode, get methods.

- For each test scenario, we can set expected behavior of validatorState: isWalkEnabled false (so schema.validate called). isValidationEnabled maybe true.

- For schema.validate return sets: emptySet for match; non-empty set for not match.

- For schema.walk called when isWalkEnabled true; we can test that path.

- For walk method test with shouldValidateSchema false: we expect schema.walk called; we can verify.

- For preloadJsonSchema: verify each schema.initializeValidators called.

Edge Cases: ensure that when numberOfValidSchema !=1, errors added include childErrors.

We'll craft tests:

1. testConstructorBuildsSchemas: verify that validationContext.newSchema called correct number of times with appropriate paths.

2. testValidateExactlyOneValidSchema: set up two schemas, first returns errors, second returns empty; expect no errors returned; state.setMatchedNode(true) after.

3. testValidateZeroValidSchemas: both schemas return errors; expect errors set contains validationMessage (one) and childErrors (both errors). Also ensure collectorContext evaluated items cleared (maybe not verify).

4. testValidateMultipleValidSchemas: both schemas return empty; expect error message with numberOfValidSchema=2, errors contain validationMessage only.

5. testValidateFailFast: set validator.failFast true via reflection; both schemas return empty (multiple matches) leads to JsonSchemaException thrown.

6. testWalkValidateTrue: when shouldValidateSchema true, walk should delegate to validate and return its messages.

7. testWalkValidateFalse: when false, walk should invoke child schema.walk and return empty set.

8. testPreloadJsonSchema: verify initializeValidators called on each schema.

We need to import necessary packages, use MockitoAnnotations.initMocks.

Add @RunWith(MockitoJUnitRunner.class) for automatic mock injection.

Define fields: @Mock ValidationContext validationContext; @Mock JsonNode schemaNode; @Mock JsonNode childNode; @Mock ExecutionContext executionContext; @Mock CollectorContext collectorContext; @Mock Scope scope; @Mock ValidatorState validatorState; @Mock JsonSchema schema0; @Mock JsonSchema schema1; etc.

Set up in @Before: init mocks; stub collectorContext.enterDynamicScope returns scope; collectorContext.exitDynamicScope returns scope; collectorContext.get(ValidatorState.VALIDATOR_STATE_KEY) returns validatorState; validatorState.isWalkEnabled returns false; validatorState.isValidationEnabled returns true; validatorState.hasMatchedNode returns true; validatorState.setComplexValidator etc. Use doNothing for setters.

Also stub collectorContext.getEvaluatedItems returns new HashSet<>; same for getEvaluatedProperties.

Now for each test, we adjust schema behavior.

The ValidationMessage class: we can create a dummy ValidationMessage via mock or using actual implementation if accessible. We'll just mock ValidationMessage.

But buildValidationMessage() is a protected method in BaseJsonValidator (maybe). It returns ValidationMessage; we don't need to inspect content; we just verify that errors size etc.

We can assert that errors contain a ValidationMessage (any). Use assertFalse(errors.isEmpty()).
